note:
Paper 85, Team 34985. Fourteen measured regions over twelve of the twenty pages of what the
running head calls nineteen, all fourteen accounted for: eleven figure rows, three table rows, no
refusals, so unaccounted is zero and nothing is left unresolved. The paper numbers nine figures -
1 through 9 with no gap - and not one table: the word "Table" never appears in the text layer, and
the three grids are named by a title row inside the box or by the appendix heading above it.

The region pass needed no argument on this paper, which is unusual in this lane. Every region is
either a framed, pasted chart or a ruled grid, and the page-wide vector bands that wrecked papers
72 and 73 do not appear at all: the eight prose pages carry no closed rule box, so they never
become regions. What the pass did do is split one printed figure into two, and the record follows
it - Figure 5's (a) and (b) halves are two pasted bitmaps side by side with their own subcaptions
and a single caption under both, so two rows carry the identical caption text.

The repetition on the summary sheet is the finding this paper contributes to the census. The
bitmap on p1 - COST at the foot, thirty arrows through the factor boxes into "Socioeconomic
Development Index" and "Ecological Impact Index" - is the same map Figure 6 prints on p13, drawn
again with slightly different factor labels and no number, no caption and no citation. The paper
therefore carries a second, invisible copy of its central diagram where a reader is most likely to
see it, and never refers back to it from the body.

The captions fail in three different ways. Figure 5's caption and Figure 2's caption reach the
text layer with every space dropped, so both are typed from the crop - "Figure2:
GraphofthetheoreticalincomedistributionI(x)andadjustedincomedistribution" is what the layer
holds, and its last token "A(x)" is pushed onto a second line. Figure 6's caption is set inside a
sentence, with the paragraph ending p12 on "we created a map of the main factors that influence
the Socioeconomic" and resuming under the caption with "and Ecological Indices of Zambia." And
Figure 4's caption welds its two panels into one run-on line with no space between the subscript
"i" and the panel letter "B:", while Figure 9's caption promises panels that are "respectively"
D_i, E_i and S but the picture carries no panel letters, no axis titles and no y numbers at all.

What the pictures show, all of it read off the crops. Figures 1 and 3 are the same world
choropleth in the same five-step ramp, keyed inside the lower left with the words Low and High and
no numbers, and both leave their no-data countries white while the prose says they are coloured
grey. Figure 4 pairs a ninety-point tradeoff scatter with four bars whose colour code is only
recoverable from the scatter's legend. Figure 5's two halves are three-by-two blocks of
automata snapshots - wealth down the left, population down the right, Initial, 10 Years and 20
Years on the arrow between them - with class breaks printed nowhere. Figure 7 is the one honest
chart on the paper: three marked curves against a labelled investment axis, an inside legend in
the Greek alpha, and a vertical rule at the 1.2 billion budget the prose points to. Figure 8 puts
six legend entries over seven groups of paired bars and prints each alpha twice, so solid against
hatched is the only cue for decade one against decade two, and its hatched 0.5 swatch is blue
while the bars it keys are pink.

The appendix grid carries the paper's arithmetic and its arithmetic errors together: thirteen
rows for twelve numbers because row 3 is printed twice, and the birth-rate equation arriving as
".070428-5.62ln(x)" with the leading 0.5 of 0.70428 gone. Row 12's equation is a stack of three
fractions that overruns its column and prints without the summation that the prose describes.

Citation is the weakest block of this paper. Four of the nine numbered figures - 1, 2, 3 and 8 -
are never named in the prose at all; Figure 4 gets one pointer on its own page, Figure 5 two,
Figure 7 two, Figure 9 one, and Figure 6 is named twice but both times a page or more away from
the art, once on p14 with a negative lead and once on p20 from the appendix. The three grids are
cited only as "the table" and "the above table" - no grid on this paper ever carries a number, so
there is nothing to cite.
rules: Measure first, then read the pixels: the fourteen measured regions of this paper resolve into eleven figure rows and three table rows with nothing refused and nothing unaccounted, because every region here is either a framed drawing or a ruled grid [place.area_frac].

A bitmap of arrows between labelled boxes is a node-link-network and not a flowchart, and it is the family only when the arrows carry a quantity: the summary map and Figure 6 both draw COST at the foot fanning into the two index sinks [geometry.family].

Two measured regions under one printed caption are two rows, never one row with a union box: Figure 5's (a) and (b) halves each own a region and each carries the same caption verbatim [caption.verbatim].

When a caption glyph run reaches the layer with its spaces stripped, the verbatim is typed from the crop instead of quoted, and the row's source is marked accordingly; Figure 5 and Figure 2 are the only two such rows here [caption.numbering].
A caption printed inside the grid is a caption: the GWP table's title row and the top-ten grid's title row are recorded with numbering 'none' and position 'above' [caption.numbering].
An unnumbered grid with no title of its own takes its name from the appendix heading printed above it, so its caption block stays empty and its numbering is 'none' [caption.numbering].
Every key on this paper is drawn inside its picture, so legend is 'inside' on all eleven figure rows and there is not one outside legend to record [geometry.legend].

Count the physical columns, not the logical ones: the GWP grid prints four columns holding two side-by-side pairs and the ranking grid prints four country columns and no numeric column at all [table.cols].
A table whose cells are all enclosed is 'boxed', and a spanning title row makes merged_cells true, while multi-line cell contents alone do not [table.merged_cells].
Rows are counted as printed, so the appendix table's repeated row number 3 gives thirteen rows for twelve numbers [table.rows].
Choropleths here key their classes with the words Low and High and no numbers, so printed_numbers is false on both map rows [geometry.printed_numbers].
A picture with no axes at all - the two function maps - still prints no numbers and is recorded with printed_numbers false [geometry.printed_numbers].

A caption that reaches the layer only after its subscripts are split to their own line is quoted with the subscript run fused into the token the page prints, e.g. 'Impact Index Ei' [mention.lead_sentence].
An exhibit first named a page after it prints takes a negative lead_pages, so Figure 6 records -1 against a first mention on p14 [mention.lead_pages].
An exhibit the prose never names records count 0 with a null first_page and no style spelling - Figures 1, 2, 3 and 8 here [mention.count].
A caption printed inside a sentence is recorded as printed and the split paragraph declared in the row note rather than repaired [place.section_path].

tables.note: The GWP weight table, ruled as a closed box: a title row spanning all four columns, a two-line header ('Pollutant' / '100-year GWP' repeated over the right-hand pair), then THREE body rows carrying six pollutants as two side-by-side column pairs - Carbon Dioxide (CO2) 1, Methane (CH4) 28, Nitrous Oxide (N2O) 265 on the left; Hydrofluorocarbons 12400, Perfluorocompounds 11100, Sulfur Hexafluoride 23500 on the right. The pair-within-one-grid layout is what makes 3 rows read as 6 entries, so cols counts the physical four. No number, no 'Table' word, no caption outside the grid; the title is inside the box and is what this row records as its caption. Body text runs above and below the box, so the table is set mid-paragraph rather than floated.

tables.note: The ranking grid, a closed box with vertical rules on all four column boundaries: a title row spanning the width, a two-line header ('Our Di' / 'SSF Human Well-being' / 'Our Ei' / 'SSF Enviro. Well-being') and TEN body rows of country names in all four columns - no numeric column at all, which is the point of the table: it is a set of four rankings laid side by side so the reader can count the overlaps. Headers wrap internally, and the 'Our Di' header mixes italic math with roman text while the other three do not. Nothing is numbered and the prose calls it only 'the table'.

The appendix equation table: four physical columns headed '#', 'Feature', 'Inputs' and 'Equation', thirteen body rows because the row number 3 is printed twice (1, 2, 3, 3, 4 through 12). Every cell is enclosed, so the grid is boxed with vertical rules; no cell is merged, and the multi-line cell contents (long feature names, stacked fractions) are wrapping, not merging. The paper's title for it is the appendix heading 'A Equations for Iterated Function Map' printed above the grid, so the caption block is empty and the heading supplies the name. Printed damage: the birth-rate equation loses its decimal point and reads '.070428-5.62ln(x)', the fourth row reuses the number 3, 'Non-Renewable' is hyphenated as 'Renev-able' across a line break, 'ln(X)' capitalises where its neighbours use 'ln(x)', and the last four rows' equations overrun their column and stack fractions with no visible summation.
